summary: Verified privacy fix for /api/expenses/all and /api/expenses/summary. Backend: 7/7 pytest cases pass — manager (alex@acme.com) only sees claims where manager_user_id == his id (both /all and /all?scope=team return identical lists; summary counts equal /all length); non-direct-report claims (HR jordan, super_admin admin) never leak to manager. Super_admin & HR still receive org-wide list including seeded outsider claims (strictly greater than manager's list). Frontend: on /admin/expenses, manager Alex sees ONLY scope-team + scope-mine tabs, no scope-all; default active tab is scope-team. Super_admin admin@acme.com and HR jordan@acme.com show scope-all + scope-mine (no scope-team), default active tab scope-all.

Manager Alex GET /api/expenses/all == GET /api/expenses/all?scope=team (identical id sets).
Manager Alex GET /api/expenses/summary total count == len(/api/expenses/all).
Super_admin admin@acme.com /api/expenses/all length strictly > manager's length and contains all 4 seeded claims.
Super_admin summary total count > manager summary total count.
HR jordan@acme.com /api/expenses/all contains admin-authored + non-report claims (org-wide preserved).
Frontend manager Alex on /admin/expenses: scope-team + scope-mine present, scope-all ABSENT, default active = scope-team.
Frontend super_admin: scope-all + scope-mine present, scope-team ABSENT.
Frontend HR jordan: scope-all + scope-mine present, scope-team ABSENT.
critical_code_review_comments: expenses.py /all: privacy rule cleanly enforces manager_user_id==user.id regardless of scope query param — good. Consider ignoring status=='paid' vs approved separation cleanly (already ok).

get_receipt endpoint (line 382) grants any manager visibility to any receipt in the tenant — after this privacy fix it is now inconsistent: a manager can still GET /api/expenses/{id}/receipt for a claim outside their team. Recommend applying the same manager_user_id==user.id gate on /expenses/{id} and /expenses/{id}/receipt for role==manager. Not part of this scope but flagging.
Approve/Reject endpoints also do not restrict a manager to only their direct reports' claims — a manager could POST /api/expenses/{someone_else_id}/approve. Same recommendation.
